heuristic.applicability: Prefer when target_pose is finite and is the current drawer-attached observed frame, the drawer is open or partly closed, and the whole drawer/handle/block arrangement may be displaced from the demonstrations while remaining reachable. Valid early entries include a block still descending/releasing or already settled; observed examples span object z about 0.063 to 0.124 at index 900. The prior covers the entire assigned 900:1330 responsibility and all 260 actions of overlap 900:1160 with place_block_in_drawer.

handoff.entry_conditions: Drawer is open near 0.300 and target_pose is observed; at early overlap entry the block may still descend/release, while later entry has the block settled near z 0.063 and an opening/open gripper retreating.
handoff.exit_conditions: Drawer_position is below the unchanged 0.025 threshold and nearly stationary, object remains inside near z 0.063, fingers are open, and TCP has retreated high and clear near z 0.358.
handoff.failure_signatures: Object still coupled when drawer begins moving, object outside cavity, missed or open fingers at handle, drawer stalled above 0.025, object leaving the drawer, IK residual/limit failure, or hand trapped at the handle.
handoff.overlap_role: Supervise every action 900:1160 in all 12 trajectories, not just context. This 260-action overlap teaches completion of release, cavity clearance, handle approach and handle acquisition before closure.
handoff.successor_readiness: Terminal skill: report readiness only from observed closed, stationary drawer plus open, retreated hand; preserve the framework success definition.

heuristic.limitations: The covariance assumes target_pose moves rigidly with the relevant drawer frame and that handle geometry relative to it is unchanged. It does not create supervision for an object outside the cavity, a changed handle offset, severe rotation causing collision/unreachability, failed physical contact, or a jam. If target_pose is unreliable or local execution error dominates instead of scene displacement, prefer the TCP-local phase-conditioned prior. If the drawer is already partly closed or closure progress/stopping is the main ambiguity, the fixed closed-destination prior supplies the stronger progress representation. All observed runs are successful; none demonstrates recovery after losing the handle.
heuristic.pipeline_implications: No caller-supplied pose is needed: target_pose is resolved from each causal observation and again from the fresh state in decode_action. Use the unchanged DiffusionBackbone. Action dimension is 10: relative position 3 m, relative rotation 6D, gripper 1. Targets come from FK of native command labels. IK is the only Cartesian-to-native arm conversion, with convergence, residual and joint-limit diagnostics. HL should switch to this prior when drawer-frame displacement is the dominant uncertainty and should not infer contact from gripper command alone.
heuristic.rationale: Most likely failure targeted: translation or rotation of the drawer assembly, hence of the placed block and approached handle, outside the nearly fixed demonstrations. The observed target_pose tracks the articulated drawer: in demo12100 its x coordinate changes from about -0.175 at drawer_position 0.300 to 0.123 at 0.0022, while handle-contact TCP x changes from about -0.448 to -0.142. Learn each commanded Cartesian pose as T_target(current action state)^-1 T_command, with target-frame xyz, target-frame rotation in continuous 6D, and the native gripper scalar. At deployment decode against the freshly observed target_pose for every executed slot, then solve IK from freshly measured joints. Build inputs from two causal frames using TCP and object poses expressed in that same moving target frame, drawer position/velocity, qpos/qvel and finger state; retaining qpos preserves reachability/configuration dependence. This makes the demonstrated release, clearance, handle approach, push, release and retreat covariant to displacement of the drawer frame by construction, rather than expecting a network to extrapolate world coordinates. Expected benefit is displacement transfer, not observed success: demonstrations themselves contain only millimetre-scale lateral variation and do not prove it.
heuristic.statement: Moving-drawer-frame SE(3) targets for displacement-invariant release, handle approach, closure, and retreat

subgoal: Ensure the block is released inside the open drawer, retreat from the cavity, approach and grasp the drawer handle, push the drawer from about 0.30 m travel to below the 0.025 closed threshold, release the handle, and retreat to a clear final pose. The intended contact target after release is the drawer handle; at early overlap states the block may still be the object being lowered/released and must not be confused with the handle. Approximate exit: drawer_position about 0.0022, block enclosed at z=0.063, open fingers, TCP high and clear.
